reviews.title: Seems pointless
reviews.text: If you don’t pay for anything but access to the app, all you get is a pretty worthless food journal.  The gimmick, I suppose, is that the AI scans your food and calculates calories and whatnot.  It does a poor job of this—you can’t easily input your own selections (they simply don’t exist, and custom input defaults to 0 calories), so you’re always left substituting your food for some other food, meaning the numbers aren’t going to be accurate from that alone.  Then the AI guesses portions really badly, so your numbers will be wrong for that reason as well.  I can’t believe I paid money for this, and I wouldn’t recommend anyone else do it either.  There are plenty of other apps that do the same thing better, just without a cartoon raccoon.

reviews.title: One suggestion

reviews.title: I can’t believe they charge money for this…
reviews.text:
….or, more embarassingly, that Inactually paid. 

The data in the app is laughable and there is no way to create custom entries or new entries for items they don’t already have. Or, for items they have but for which their data is woefully inaccurate. I have used other apps that are far superior and that do not cost money. What they provide as a “plan” for you to follow is a generic daily calorie intake and a generic/default fasting period. The only thing this app gives me that is in any way different is the raccoon — which doesn’t impress me enough to pay for this. I expect to go back to the apps I have used before and ignore this one, despite having three and a half weeks left of my four week “plan.” 

If anyone thinks they are going to get accurate information from a picture of your plate and an AI estimate, think again. I mean, I knew the AI picture thing does not work, but I had thought I would be able to enter my own data.

I was hoping good things would come from using this app. After using it for a day, I realized it was falling short. You don't receive accurate info on calories by letting AI analyze your pictures of food. The inability of scanning barcodes was a zero for me. Editing info is a challenge.

I requested a refund and that was difficult. They had no record of me purchasing the app even though I had proof from my credit card statement. They wanted the last four digits of my card number which I declined to give. I contacted Apple support and sent them print screens of the purchase. I was going to dispute the credit card charge with bank than in the middle of the night my purchase was refunded. Then they asked for a review which isn't happening.

Their email address can be located by going to the settings wheel or by going to their website to request a refund. Good luck.
